export_blockers.description: InferenceCore accumulates per-object memory (object_logits, long_term_memory, etc.) across frames via repeated step() calls. Each step() depends on state built by previous steps. Export requires capturing the entire step loop or flattening the state machine.

MatAnyone2 inference uses a Python-level frame loop with warmup, first-frame masking, and continuation steps. The loop has branches (first_frame_pred, mask provision) that depend on frame index. Not directly representable as a single static graph.

Frames and masks can have arbitrary spatial dimensions. Model internal tensors (object logits, memory) are sized dynamically based on input. ONNX/TorchScript export typically requires fixed or explicitly-dynamic dimension declarations.

InferenceCore stores configuration objects, integer counters, and potentially dicts/lists of tensors as temporal state. Pure tensor-export formats (ONNX, TorchScript) cannot directly represent this mixed Python/tensor state.
The worker divides pixel values by 255.0 (uint8→float normalization) and permutes HWC→CHW before feeding to model. Export must include or exclude this preprocessing consistently.
Alpha masks are extracted via output_prob_to_mask(), then scaled to 0-255 uint8 and saved as PNG. This post-processing is Python-side and would need separate handling in any exported runtime.
The worker feeds the first frame N=10 times as warmup before real inference. This stabilises temporal memory but adds latency. Export must account for or skip this warmup phase.
